'''Michael Smolensky''' is an American [[Chronobiology|chronobiologist]] working in [[hypertension]] and [[pathophysiology]].

==Education and career==
He earned his Ph.D at [[University of Illinois]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://directory.utexas.edu/index.php?q=smolensky&scope=all&submit=Search |title=Michael H. Smolensky |publisher=utexas.edu |accessdate=December 27, 2017}}</ref>

He founded and for 10 years directed the Memorial-Hermann Center for [[Chronobiology]] and [[Chronotherapeutics]] (the first polyclinic to use biological rhythm to diagnose and cure disease).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/ntp/roc/meetings/2016/alan/shortbios20160310_508.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161105055941/http://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/ntp/roc/meetings/2016/alan/shortbios20160310_508.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 5, 2016 |title=Bios |publisher=nih.gov |accessdate=December 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/03/06/us/new-drugs-are-precisely-timed-to-match-body-s-biological-clock.html |title=New Drugs Are Precisely Timed To Match Body's Biological Clock |date=March 6, 1996 |work=[[The New York Times]] |accessdate=December 27, 2017}}</ref>

He is the author or co-author of more than 300 academic articles; his highest cited paper is "Ethics and methods for biological rhythm research on animals and human beings".<ref>Francesco Portaluppi, Michael H. Smolensky, Yvan Touitou. Ethics and methods for biological rhythm research on animals and human beings. The Journal of Biological and Medical Rhythm Research
Volume 27, 2010 - Issue 9-10 1911-1929</ref> at 739 times, according to [[Google Scholar]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C44&q=Michael+Smolensky&btnG=|title=Michael Smolensky|accessdate=December 27, 2017}}</ref> He also co-authored (alongside [[Lynne Lamberg]]) the book ''The Body Clock Guide to Better Health'' which is held in 449 libraries.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n83049831/ |title=Smolensky, Michael H. |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=December 27, 2017}}</ref>

He recently was involved in works upon resilience and circadian reliability of fire departments with French [[firefighters]].<ref name="AE Al. 2017">{{Cite journal| last=AE | first=Reinberg  |date=December 28, 2017 | pmid=28920706 | title=Do night and around-the-clock firefighters' shift schedules induce deviation in tau from 24 hours of systolic and diastolic blood pressure circadian rhythms? | journal=Chronobiology International | volume=34 | issue=8 | pages=1158–1174 | doi=10.1080/07420528.2017.1343833 | s2cid=1490115 }}</ref><ref name="Y Al. 2017">{{Cite journal| last=Y | first=Touitou  | date=December 28, 2017 | pmid=24851404 | title=Twenty-four-hour pattern in French firemen of lag time response to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and work-related injury  | journal=Indian Journal of Experimental Biology  | volume=52  | issue=5  | pages=420–4  }}</ref><ref name="M Al. 2004">{{Cite journal| last=M | first=Riedel | date=December 1, 2003 | pmid=21929300 | title=24-hour pattern of work-related injury risk of French firemen: Nocturnal peak time | journal=Chronobiology International | volume=28 | issue=8 | pages=697–705 | doi=10.3109/07420528.2011.603170 | s2cid=33014574 }}</ref>
